answer: The protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by enforcing a timber-bonded reputation model where voting rights require lock-ups of timber tokens. These assets are secured within a lotus smart contract, verified by the mesa optimizer which cross-validates node diversity against token distribution. Any divergence indicates fraud, triggering liquidation of the locked timber. Thus, attackers must procure resources proportional to desired hash power, raising the marginal cost of creating identities to a threshold that exceeds potential short-term gains, rendering the attack economically prohibitive.
